From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@flowpay.com
Date: 2026-08-01T02:10:00Z
Subject: Re: FlowPay - 429/5xx spike — initial triage

Quick update from infra: we are seeing a pattern of short-lived TCP resets and 502/503 translations from the FastEdge CDN in front of FlowPay. Key findings so far:
- Connection attempts from several of our GCP egress IPs are being rate-limited/blocked by the CDN after repeated retries.
- There's a cluster of failures that coincide with GCP Cloud NAT IP rotation events in us-central1 (~2026-08-01T00:50-01:00Z).
- Retry amplification observed: our HTTP clients retry on 502/timeout and the CDN/client then returns 429 due to per-IP thresholds.

Immediate mitigations we can try (short-lived):
1) Reduce client-side retry multiplier and backoff to avoid amplifying the failure.
2) Temporarily route affected workload through an alternate egress (aws-us-east-1) if available.
3) Ask FlowPay to whitelist the currently active Redwood egress IP range or allowlist ASN.

I'll attach a screenshot of the NAT event correlation and a brief packet-level sample.

Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: nat-rotation-screenshot.png (image)]

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-01T03:10:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Exec notice — FlowPay degraded, customer facing and mitigation plan

Folks — escalating for visibility. FlowPay (large payments customer) is experiencing sustained 429/5xx for transactions served through their FastEdge CDN; suspected root cause is GCP Cloud NAT egress rotation triggering per-IP throttling at the CDN and causing retry storms from our clients.

Customer impact: increased latency and failed transaction density for a subset of tenants routing through us-central1. FlowPay is rehearsing their capacity to whitelist, but this is causing customer-visible failures now.

Actions taken so far:
- Vivek correlated GCP NAT rotation timestamps with our error spike.
- Reduced default client retry window on the affected service (deployed - rollback ready).
- Requested FlowPay whitelist our egress IP range with FastEdge.

Requested from leadership:
- Approval to failover affected routes to AWS us-east-1 for the next 24 hours (cost and routing implications noted).
- Communicate an incident timeline and ETA to FlowPay (Ben to own customer comms).

I can be on the call with FlowPay and their CDN if needed.

Irene

From: gcp-support@google.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Support case 123456789 — Cloud NAT IP rotation diagnostics

Hello Vivek / Irene,

We investigated case 123456789. There was a brief burst of Cloud NAT ephemeral IP reassignments in us-central1 between 2026-08-01T00:45 and 2026-08-01T01:05 UTC due to an internal autoscaling event on a shared NAT pool. While NAT behavior was within expected parameters, we see that several flows experienced transient source-IP changes which can trigger per-IP limits on some CDNs. Engineering has recommended the following:
- Use a dedicated Cloud NAT or reserved egress IPs for predictable source IPs.
- Open a fast-track support case with FastEdge to coordinate throttling thresholds and temporary allowlist.

We've moved the case to high priority and attached packet-level correlation logs. Please let us know if you'd like GCP on a triage call with FastEdge and FlowPay.

Best,
GCP Support Team

[Attachment: gcp-nat-correlation.tar.gz (logs)]

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: ops@flowpay.com, irene.choi@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T18:45:00Z
Subject: RESOLVED: FlowPay - 429/5xx spike (mitigation summary & next steps)

FlowPay / Team —

Thanks for working through this. Summary and closure notes:
- Root cause: transient Cloud NAT egress IP rotations in GCP caused multiple Redwood flows to change source IPs, triggering per-IP throttling at the FastEdge CDN in front of FlowPay. This, combined with aggressive client retries, produced a retry storm and elevated 429/5xx rates.
- Immediate mitigations applied: reduced client retries, temporary regional failover to aws-us-east-1 for the most impacted tenant traffic, FlowPay requested FastEdge to allowlist current Redwood ASN for 24h.
- Outcome: error rate returned to baseline by 2026-08-02T18:20:00Z. FlowPay confirms normal traffic.

Next steps / longer term:
- Implement reserved/persistent egress IPs (Cloud NAT dedicated) for FlowPay-dedicated routes.
- Add RFC to the infra backlog to make retry throttling adaptive based on upstream indicators (INC-1245).
- Schedule a postmortem with FlowPay and FastEdge this week — propose 2026-08-04 17:00 UTC.

Attachments: rfc-failover-plan.docx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
